implementation_notes: Both dominant TypeScript ORMs implement the token declaratively: TypeORM's @VersionColumn is an automatically incremented column and repository.findOne({ lock: { mode: 'optimistic', version } }) re-checks it against the value you loaded, failing with an optimistic-lock version mismatch when the row moved on; MikroORM documents automatic optimistic locking through a version field it bumps and compares on flush. The decorator replaces the hand-written predicate, and what remains yours is the conflict policy - reload and merge, retry the unit of work, or answer 409. In driver-level code (pg, mysql2) the token does not exist, so keep WHERE id = $1 AND version = $2 and the rowCount test by hand, and in clients without a version feature (for example Prisma) manage field and predicate yourself.
pitfalls: repo.update()/updateMany() and QueryBuilder bulk statements skip @VersionColumn bookkeeping; the token is only maintained on save/upsert paths.
The optimistic lock only fires when the lock option (with the version you read) is passed - omitting it silently updates the row.
Long-lived transactions that await user input hold connections; read, release, then re-check the version on the write instead.
Clients with no version feature (Prisma, raw drivers) require field and predicate to be maintained by hand - do not assume the ORM covers it.

variants.name: MikroORM version property with automatic optimistic locking
variants.implementation_notes: MikroORM documents automatic optimistic locking through a version field declared on the entity: the ORM bumps the field and compares the loaded value at flush time, so the token stays in the unit of work rather than in the query. It is the alternative to TypeORM's decorator for teams already on MikroORM's identity-map-based EntityManager, and it composes with its transactional API. As with every ORM-managed token, the check applies only to writes the ORM flushes; custom queries and bulk statements remain the application's responsibility.
pitfalls: The check runs at flush time, so a long unit of work can hold a stale entity across unrelated changes and report the conflict late.
MongoDB documents in MikroORM have their own version nuances; verify the version field is persisted for the driver you use.
